meta.title: Texas school vouchers, 10 days of posts
meta.subject: Texas school vouchers and education savings accounts (ESAs) — the state program, its rollout, costs and effect on public schools
meta.subtitle: Oct 6 to Oct 15, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas school vouchers, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Vouchers are a GOP electoral liability
lanes.description: Vouchers and school funding fights are costing Republicans suburban and rural voters and could help Democrats win Texas races, including the governor's race.

lanes.label: Vouchers drain rural and public schools
lanes.description: Vouchers and school funding cuts are squeezing public school districts, especially rural ones where the district is the biggest employer, and are hurting staff and budgets.

lanes.label: TEFA is working for families
lanes.description: The Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program is delivering on its promises, helping over 100,000 kids including special-needs students, and mostly serving middle- and lower-income families.

lanes.label: Choice funded separately, not from schools
lanes.description: Pro-voucher voices say school choice takes no money from public schools because TEFA is funded by a separate General Revenue appropriation, and credit GOP leaders for parental rights and school choice.

lanes.label: Taxpayer giveaway to rich and religious
lanes.description: Vouchers redistribute taxpayer money to wealthy families and private religious schools that can discriminate, rather than serving ordinary Texas students.

lanes.label: Focus on learning outcomes and accountability
lanes.description: Voters care more about whether kids read and do math at grade level than about the school choice fight, so accountability and proficiency should drive education policy.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.name: Senator Ted Cruz
posts.text:
Mark, it’s disappointing to see you parroting the teachers unions’ misleading talking points about school choice. Let’s set the record straight.

First, my legislation creates scholarships funded by private donations, without taking a dime from public schools. Not one dollar is diverted from Arizona’s existing public-school funding. The claim that this program defunds Arizona schools is flatly false.

Second, these scholarships benefit children in public and private schools. Governors from Texas to Colorado to New York have opted in, including Democrat Gov. Kathy Hochul, because they realize this program will unleash billions of dollars to kids across their states.

If Arizona refuses to participate, Arizona taxpayers can still claim the federal tax credit by contributing to eligible scholarship organizations in other states. Arizona taxpayers will help educate kids in Texas, New York, and Colorado while Arizona kids are denied the same opportunity.

I’d encourage you to spend less time repeating teachers union talking points and more time reading what the law actually says. 

We saw during COVID what happens when politicians put the demands of teachers unions ahead of the needs of children. Arizona kids deserve better.

posts.name: Jan Jekielek
posts.text:
For decades, Texas governors tried and failed to pass school choice.

Governor Greg Abbott finally got it done, and he told me what that moment felt like.

“Governors going back to George W. Bush, to Rick Perry, and to myself earlier in my career, fought to provide school choice for the kids of Texas, and always it was insurmountable.”

“I had to campaign across the entire state to get enough votes in the Texas legislature to get it across the finish line.”

“This is a multi-decade event.”

“To finally get that across the finish line, sign it into law, surrounded by parents who were crying because finally they had the opportunity to choose the education pathway that’s best for their child, was really kind of emotionally wrenching.”

@GregAbbott_TX
